findings.F1: Larger falls are not followed by larger rebounds over 2 days. Down days of -0.75 to -1.5 usual moves are followed by +0.80 % above drift (t 1.95, 847 cases), -1.5 to -2.5 by +0.64 % (t 1.17, 333), and beyond -2.5 by +0.69 % (t 0.77, 81). The pooled slope on down days alone (-0.620 % per unit, t -2.26, 3536 cases on 940 days) rests on the mildest falls, not on the largest.
findings.F2: Streak length gives no graded follow-on move. At 2 days every streak bucket from -5 to +5 has |t| under 1.6. At 5 days only the 4-down streak stands out (-4.25 %, t -2.36, 80 cases), while 3-down gives +1.41 % (t 1.29) and 5-down -0.92 % (t -0.41). The pattern is not monotone, so it reads as chance.
findings.F3: Short-term against long-term volatility (log of the 10-day over the 60-day std) has a 2-day slope of +0.738 % per unit (t 2.10, 7210 cases, 1265 days). It fades to t 1.57 at 5 days and t -0.08 at 10 days. Per coin it reaches |t| above 2 only on XRP (2.16) and ZEC (2.34), with BTC at -0.47 and XMR at -0.38.
findings.F4: The 20-day volatility-scaled return has a 10-day slope of +0.942 % (t 1.35, 1403 cases), but its sign changes by year: 2023 t -2.67, 2022 t -1.46, 2018 t -1.33, 2024 t +1.11. The 5-day return shows the same weakness (t 1.93 at 10 days, 255 days).
findings.F5: Next-day excess return by weekday is significant on Friday only (+0.31 %, t 2.09, 2479 cases). The other six days all have |t| at or under 1.30, which is what chance gives among seven groups.
findings.F6: The book tracks the coins. Its daily correlation with the coins' mean return is 0.74. On its worst 2 % of days it loses 6.9 % while the coins lose 10.3 %; on its best 2 % it gains 6.4 % while they gain 8.9 %. Its large moves are the market's moves, scaled by about 0.7.
findings.F7: The rebound after falls beyond 1.5 usual moves is not reliable in any single slice. By year it is positive in 6 of 8 years, but no year has t above 1.42 (2018 -0.65 %, 2025 -0.36 %). By coin it ranges from ETH -0.06 % (t -0.10) to LTC +1.71 % (t 1.89).

no_ideas: Across roughly forty angles (scaled 1-, 5- and 20-day returns at 2, 5 and 10 days, streak length, volatility ratio, 20-day return quintiles, weekday, year, coin, and the book's extreme days), the best patterns reach t of only about 2.1 to 2.4. That is what that many looks produce by chance, and none of them grows steadily with its situation or holds across years and coins, so none can carry a new idea.
